homeQuote.alt: The Albir Family - Three Generations at Cafetos de Segovia
homeQuote.quote: At Cafetos de Segovia, we are committed to integrity, transparency, and excellence. From cultivation to export, every stage of our specialty green coffee process is traceable and intentional. The exceptional flavor in every cup reflects our passion for natural process coffees and the purity of the Nicaragua origin.

beneficio.title: From cherry to container, under one roof
beneficio.text: Every lot we export passes through our own beneficio in Nueva Segovia. Drying, milling, sorting, storage and cupping happen in one place, run by our own team, so we control each step and can tell you exactly where your coffee has been.

steps.title: Drying
steps.text: Washed and honey coffees dry in parchment on raised beds, and naturals in the full cherry. Our team turns every bed by hand throughout the day for slow, even drying.

steps.title: Milling & sorting
steps.text: Hulling, size grading and optical color sorting remove defects before a lot is approved.

steps.title: Lot storage
steps.text: Each lot rests separately, tagged with its farm, process and date, so it stays traceable to export.

steps.title: Cupping lab
steps.text: Every lot is cupped in our own lab before it is offered, and again before it ships.

services.title: From origin to destination
services.intro: We are producers ourselves, and we have been exporting Nicaraguan coffee for more than twelve years. That experience lets us work on both ends of the chain: growing alongside the producers of Nueva Segovia, and preparing their coffee for roasters around the world. Everything in between happens at our own dry mill, with our own team.

producers.title: Growing with producers
producers.text: We grow coffee on our own family farms, so we know what each season asks of a producer. We share that experience with our partner producers, from the field to the cupping table, so every harvest can show its full potential.
producers.alt: Two women with a coffee seedling
items: Practical advice on harvest, shade, pruning and fertilization, based on what works on our own farms.
Fermentation and drying methods we test on our farms first, then share.
An evaluation of every lot, to understand its profile and how to improve it.
Coffee presented to importers and roasters in Europe, the US, Asia, Australia and the Middle East.

export.title: Export-ready coffee
export.text: Every lot that leaves our mill is separated, cupped and documented. From microlots to full containers, specialty and commercial, we take care of selection, preparation and export, so the coffee arrives as it was cupped at origin.
items: Lots from our family farms and partner producers, matched to each roaster's profile.
Pre-shipment samples and a cupping report for every lot.
Farm geolocation and a traceability sheet per lot, ready for the European market.
Packing, documentation, customs and shipping, with farm visits on request.

process.title: From cherry to container, step by step
process.exportAlt: Coffee lots prepared at our dry mill for export
process.note: Honey water from washing goes to treatment piles away from water sources, protecting the rivers of the Dipilto-Jalapa reserve.
steps: Only fully ripe cherries are hand-picked, then sorted and floated in clean water to remove defects.
Washed coffees ferment 18 to 36 hours before washing in channels with clean water. Anaerobic lots rest in sealed barrels for 48 to 140 hours, with temperature and pH monitored throughout.
Slow drying on raised African beds, alternating sun and ventilated shade: about 12 days for washed coffees and 28 days for naturals, until the coffee reaches 12% moisture.
Lots rest in our warehouse to stabilize before milling, each one identified by farm, variety and process.
Every lot is roasted, cupped and scored in our lab, and its moisture and physical quality are checked.
Hulling, screen-size grading, density sorting, optical color sorting and a final hand-picking of defects.
Coffee is packed to each roaster's specification and labeled for full traceability.
Documentation, customs clearance, freight booking and follow-up until the coffee arrives.

about.subtitle: Three generations of coffee excellence from the highlands of Nueva Segovia

values.title: HERITAGE
values.content: Cafetos de Segovia was founded by Ana and Martha Albir, representing the third generation of their family's coffee legacy. We bridge tradition with innovation, providing transparent and socially responsible connections to Nicaraguan coffee farmers. Our passionate team of specialists ensures the highest quality standards throughout the entire production chain, building lasting relationships with partner farms and buyers worldwide.

values.title: OUR COFFEE
values.content: We partner with exceptional farmers to navigate changing environmental conditions while preserving traditional farming culture. Our collaboration with outstanding importers and roasters focuses on sustainability and quality excellence. Through innovative micro-milling and advanced processing techniques, we enhance flavors and maintain consistency. Every cup tells the story of dedicated farmers and our commitment to environmental stewardship.

values.title: SUSTAINABILITY
values.content: At Cafetos de Segovia, sustainability is our foundation. We cultivate coffee with deep reverence for the terroir, implementing practices that preserve our environment for future generations. Our connection with nature defines our identity and legacy, ensuring that every bean reflects our commitment to responsible farming and environmental protection.

values.title: INNOVATION
values.content: Innovation drives our pursuit of excellence in specialty coffee. We continuously explore cutting-edge processing methods and quality enhancement techniques. Our commitment to creativity and pioneering approaches ensures we deliver exceptional coffee experiences while maintaining the highest standards of consistency and flavor development.

values.title: DRYING & PROCESSING
values.content:
Drying is where a good harvest is protected or lost, so we take it slowly. After processing, our coffee rests on raised beds in the open air, where it dries evenly with the sun and the mountain breeze. Our team turns every bed by hand several times a day and checks moisture until each lot reaches the right level for storage and export.

Natural, honey and washed lots dry separately, and every bed is identified by farm and process. That way each lot keeps its own character and its own traceability, from the farm to the bag.

values.title: LABORATORY & QUALITY CONTROL
values.content:
Every lot is evaluated in our own cupping lab before we offer it. We roast samples, cup them blind alongside our reference lots, and score each one, so we know exactly what is in every bag before a buyer tastes it.

Alongside cupping, we check moisture and the physical quality of the green coffee, looking for defects, size and uniformity. Only lots that meet our standards are prepared for export, and we cup them again before they ship.

farmsPage.subtitle: A selection of the farms we work with, from a network of more than 40 in northern Nicaragua.
farmsPage.quote: We value sustainability, innovation, and the people who make every harvest possible.
farmsPage.partnerText: Beyond the farms shown here, our network includes more than 40 partner farms in Dipilto, Mozonte, San Fernando and Macuelizo. Lots from these farms are available on request, with the same care and traceability.
farmsPage.originsIntro: From Nueva Segovia to Jinotega, in the coffee highlands of northern Nicaragua.

areas.label: Dipilto, Nueva Segovia
areas.heading: The highlands of the Serranías de Dipilto y Jalapa
areas.text: On the border with Honduras, inside the Serranías de Dipilto y Jalapa Nature Reserve. Steep slopes, pine and cloud forest, and cool nights give slow-ripening cherries and clean, sweet, structured cups.

areas.label: Mozonte, Nueva Segovia
areas.heading: The highlands of Mozonte
areas.text: East of Ocotal, where the land rises to more than 1,800 metres. Forested highlands that hold the springs of the Mozonte river and give dense beans with bright acidity.

areas.label: Macuelizo, Nueva Segovia
areas.heading: The highlands of Macuelizo
areas.text: West of Ocotal, in quieter highlands between 1,300 and 1,500 metres, where shade-grown coffee and family tradition go back generations.

areas.label: JINOTEGA, NICARAGUA
areas.heading: The mountains of Jinotega
areas.text: One of Nicaragua's main coffee regions, in the central-northern highlands. Misty mountains and fertile soils produce balanced cups with body and sweetness.

farmsPage.closingText: Experience the exceptional quality of our farm-specific lots.
farmsPage.ownText: These two farms belong to Ana and Martha Albir, the sisters who founded Cafetos de Segovia. They are where our family's story with coffee began, and where we first test new varieties and processes.
farmsPage.networkTitle: A few of our 40+ partner farms
farmsPage.networkText: We work with more than 40 partner farms in Nueva Segovia, many of them family relations and long-standing neighbours. Here are a few of them.

agua-sarca.description: Agua Sarca has been run by the same family for more than thirty years. Set on sandy-loam soils with steady rainfall and cool highland air, it grows coffee under an agroforestry canopy of native trees, fruit trees and bananas, with native forest reserves kept across the estate.
agua-sarca.varieties: Red & Yellow Catuaí, Caturra, Maracaturra, Pacamara, Ovata, Marsellesa, Parainema, Geisha
agua-sarca.difference: Its widest collection of varieties, and a Cup of Excellence Nicaragua finalist repeatedly since 2017.

la-picona.description: La Picona is the only coffee farm on Picona Mountain. A woman-led farm, it grows all its coffee under full shade of guaba, búcaro, cedar and banana trees, on sandy, mineral-rich volcanic soil. Cool breezes and wide swings between day and night temperatures slow down ripening.
la-picona.size: 7 ha, including 2 ha of conserved native forest
la-picona.varieties: Maracaturra, Parainema, Sidra, Java, Catuaí, young Geisha plants
la-picona.difference: 2nd place in the Cup of Excellence Nicaragua 2021 with a Maracaturra anaerobic honey.

mirjam.description: Morning mist, a steady breeze and fertile volcanic-influenced soil shape the coffee at Mirjam, all grown under full shade. A micro-lot program starts with the 2026 harvest.
mirjam.size: 27 ha, including 3.5 ha of conserved native forest
mirjam.difference: One of the richest bird populations in the region, with toucans, hummingbirds and tanagers among the coffee. Recognized several times in the Cup of Excellence Nicaragua.
mirjam.development: Sidra, Geisha, Chiroso, Arará, Pink Bourbon

el-cipres.description: El Ciprés has been run by its current owner since 2013. About a third of the land is left as natural forest, protecting water sources, flora and wildlife, within the Serranías de Dipilto-Jalapa Nature Reserve.
el-cipres.size: 21 ha, about a third kept as natural forest
el-cipres.difference: Planted with newer, resilient varieties like Parainema, Marsellesa and Ovata, explored through natural and anaerobic processes.

bethania.description: Bethania belongs to Martha Albir, co-founder of Cafetos de Segovia. It has passed from generation to generation in the Albir family, and she has run it since 1991. Coffee grows under forest, fruit and banana shade, with regular pruning and shade management to bring light into the plantation.
bethania.varieties: Catimor, Red & Yellow Catuaí, Java, Maracaturra, Pacamara
bethania.difference: Home to Java and Pacamara, and to long anaerobic naturals fermented in sealed barrels while temperature and pH are monitored.
bethania.development: Sidra, Geisha, Chiroso, Arará, Pink Bourbon

las-hortensias.description: Las Hortensias belongs to Ana Albir, co-founder of Cafetos de Segovia, and has been in the family for more than fifty years. A small farm where coffee grows under forest, fruit and banana shade, picked only when fully ripe, then sorted and floated before processing.
las-hortensias.difference: Its Marsellesa is processed both washed and as a 96-hour anaerobic natural, showing how much process can change the same variety.

nicaragua.title: Nicaragua
nicaragua.subtitle: What makes Nicaragua special as a coffee origin

sections.title: A country shaped by coffee
sections.text: Coffee is one of Nicaragua's most important exports and the livelihood of thousands of families, most of them small and medium producers. Almost all of it is arabica, grown in the cool mountains of the north, where altitude, volcanic soils and a clear dry season give the beans their density and sweetness.

sections.title: Mountains, mist and a real dry season
sections.text: The coffee regions of the north sit between roughly 1,000 and 1,800 metres. Cool nights slow the ripening of the cherry, which builds sugars and acidity, and a long dry season from November to April makes slow, careful sun drying possible. Most coffee here grows under shade, among native trees, fruit trees and bananas.

sections.title: Nueva Segovia, the northernmost coffee region
sections.text: Nueva Segovia borders Honduras and is home to the Serranías de Dipilto y Jalapa nature reserve, where many of our farms and partner producers grow coffee. The region is known for clean, sweet and structured cups, and its coffees regularly stand out in the Cup of Excellence Nicaragua, including lots from our own family farms.
facts: Municipalities: Dipilto, Mozonte, Macuelizo, San Fernando

sections.title: From classic varieties to new expressions
sections.text: Caturra, Red and Yellow Catuaí and Maracaturra, the large-bean variety Nicaragua is known for, grow alongside newer and rarer varieties such as Java, Pacamara, Parainema, Marsellesa and Geisha. Washed coffee remains the tradition, while naturals, honeys and anaerobic fermentations open new profiles every harvest.

sections.title: From the mountain to the port
sections.text: Cherries are picked by hand, processed at the farm or the wet mill, and brought down as parchment to dry mills like ours. There the coffee is dried, rested, milled, sorted and cupped before it leaves by truck for the port and, from there, for roasters around the world.
